2027-04-26.title: Fifth Monday of Resurrection
2027-04-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal
2027-04-26.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost.
2027-04-26.verse: For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.
theo: The crowds around Jesus keep growing, and with the crowds grows the demand for proof. They want a sign from heaven, something so overwhelming that no one could doubt. Jesus refuses: “This generation is an evil generation; it asks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.” Then he explains: “For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.” What was the sign of Jonah? A prophet who went down into the depths, swallowed up as if dead, and came back after three days to preach. Matthew spells it out: “For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth” (Matthew 12:40). We read this Gospel four weeks after Easter, and so we hear it as the disciples heard it after the Resurrection: the sign has been given. The tomb is empty. There will be no other sign greater than this one, and no sign is needed beyond it. The Church still meets people who ask for a proof that would force them to believe. She can only point, as Jesus did, to the Crucified One who rose on the third day, and to the lives of those who have met him.

Jesus then names two foreigners who will rise at the judgment and put his hearers to shame. The queen of the South travelled from the ends of the earth just to listen to Solomon's wisdom; the people of Nineveh, a pagan city, “repented at the proclamation of Jonah”. And the refrain comes twice: “see, something greater than Solomon is here!”, “see, something greater than Jonah is here!” Jesus does not speak against his own people; he speaks as a prophet of Israel, calling his generation to listen as Nineveh listened. Every generation, ours included, is in the same place. Our Syro-Malabar Church keeps the memory of Nineveh alive every year in the Moonnu Nombu, the three days' fast of the Ninevites before the Great Fast, when the faithful flock to Kuravilangad and to many other churches and fast with the hope of the people who believed a preacher of repentance. Today, in the bright weeks of Easter, the same story speaks of joy rather than sackcloth: if Nineveh changed at the voice of Jonah, how much more should we change at the voice of the One who came back from the dead, greater than Jonah and greater than Solomon.

Peter writes to Christians who are discovering that the Risen Lord does not take them out of trouble. “Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal that is taking place among you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.” Suffering for Christ is not a sign that something has gone wrong; it is part of belonging to him. “But rejoice insofar as you are sharing Christ's sufferings, so that you may also be glad and shout for joy when his glory is revealed.” The joy of Easter is not cancelled by the Cross; it shines through it. Peter is precise: there is no glory in suffering for doing wrong, but “if any of you suffers as a Christian, do not consider it a disgrace, but glorify God because you bear this name.” The name Christian, first given at Antioch (Acts 11:26), was perhaps meant as mockery; the martyrs wore it as a crown. The fiery ordeal comes in many sizes: the student laughed at for making the sign of the Cross before a meal, the employee passed over for refusing to falsify an account, the believers in many lands who lose homes and lives for the faith. To all of them Peter gives one instruction: “let those suffering in accordance with God's will entrust themselves to a faithful Creator, while continuing to do good.” Entrust, and keep doing good. That is how the sign of Jonah is lived in an ordinary Christian life: going down into trouble without losing faith, and coming up again with the light of the Resurrection.
outline: Ask: what sign am I still waiting for before I give myself fully to Christ?
Point 1 · No sign but the sign of Jonah
Three days in the depths, and the empty tomb.
Nineveh repented, the queen came from afar; what about us?
Point 3 · Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal
Suffering as a Christian, and entrusting ourselves to a faithful Creator.
“See, something greater than Jonah is here!”
live: Make an act of faith today in the Risen Lord, without conditions: Lord, you are risen; that is enough for me.
Bear the name with joy (1 Peter 4:16)
Make the sign of the Cross openly before one meal today, wherever you are, and pray for Christians who suffer for the name.
fathers: Jonah was cast into the belly of the great fish, but Christ went down of his own will into the heart of the earth. Jonah was brought up again to preach repentance to Nineveh; Christ rose to call the whole world to repentance and life. If the story of Jonah is believed, how much more the Resurrection of the Lord.

On his way to martyrdom he begged the Christians of Rome not to prevent his death: let me be food for the beasts, through whom I may reach God. I am the wheat of God, ground by their teeth, that I may be found the pure bread of Christ.
magis: Jesus links faith in the resurrection to his own person and gives the sign of Jonah, the sign of the temple, as the sign of his own Resurrection.
Interior repentance is a radical reorientation of our whole life, a return to God with all our heart, as Nineveh turned at the preaching of Jonah.
Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith; the martyr bears witness to Christ who died and rose, to whom he is united by charity.
2027-04-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you went down into the heart of the earth and rose on the third day: you are the sign of Jonah given to every generation. Forgive us for asking for more proof when you have already given us yourself. Give us the humility of Nineveh to repent at your word, and the courage of your martyrs to bear your name without shame. When the fiery ordeal comes, teach us to entrust ourselves to the faithful Creator and to go on doing good, until your glory is revealed and we shout for joy. Amen. Alleluia!
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the sign of Jonah placed in our hands: the Lord who went down into death and rose again gives us his Body and Blood. Something greater than Solomon and greater than Jonah is here on the altar.

quick: Jesus refuses every sign but the sign of Jonah: his death and Resurrection on the third day.
Nineveh repented at Jonah's voice; something greater than Jonah is here.
Peter: do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal; if you suffer as a Christian, glorify God for the name.
2027-04-26.action: Make the sign of the Cross openly before a meal today, and pray for persecuted Christians.
2027-04-26.question: Am I still waiting for a sign, when the Risen Lord has already been given to me?

family.explain: Long ago God sent the prophet Jonah to a big city called Nineveh. Jonah was swallowed by a huge fish and after three days he came out again and preached to the city. The people listened, said sorry to God and changed their lives. Jesus said that he would be like Jonah: he would be in the tomb for three days and then rise again. And he did! That is the biggest sign God has given us.
family.intention: We pray for Christians around the world who are laughed at or hurt because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we need to say sorry to God for, like the people of Nineveh?”

illus: A young engineer from Kanjirappally joined a company in Bengaluru and shared a flat with five colleagues. On the first evening he quietly made the sign of the Cross before eating, and the others laughed. For weeks he was ‘the Father’ of the flat. He did not argue and did not stop. Months later, when one of his flatmates lost his mother, it was this young man he knocked on the door of at midnight. ‘You pray,’ he said. ‘Please pray for her.’ They prayed together, and the next morning the friend asked him to explain what Christians believe about the dead. The young man said afterwards that the laughter had been the small price; the midnight knock was the reward.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you are the sign given to our generation. Open our hearts as we gather in your name. Amen. Alleluia!
share: No sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Luke 11:29). What signs or proofs do I still demand of God?
The people of Nineveh repented at the proclamation of Jonah (Luke 11:32). Where is the Lord calling me to change?
Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal (1 Peter 4:12). What trial am I going through for my faith?
Entrust themselves to a faithful Creator, while continuing to do good (1 Peter 4:19). How can I go on doing good in my difficulty?
pm.resp: Lord, greater than Jonah, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the Risen Christ as the one sign given to the world.
For Christians who suffer for the name of Christ in India and in every land, that they may be strong and joyful.
For those who persecute believers, that their hearts may be turned to peace.
For those who are searching for God and asking for signs, that they may meet the Risen Lord.
For our families, that we may repent and believe like the people of Nineveh.
pm.close: Father, you gave the sign of Jonah when you raised your Son from the heart of the earth. Make us believe without demanding more, repent without delay, and suffer without shame for the name we bear. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, the crowds around Jesus wanted a sign, a great proof from heaven. Jesus said: no sign will be given to this generation except the sign of Jonah (Luke 11:29).

Jonah was three days in the belly of the great fish, and then came out and preached. Jesus was three days in the heart of the earth, and then rose. We are in the season of the Resurrection: the sign has been given. The tomb is empty.

The people of Nineveh, a pagan city, repented at the preaching of Jonah. The queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon. And Jesus says: something greater than Jonah is here, something greater than Solomon is here (Luke 11:31–32). Our Church remembers Nineveh every year in the Moonnu Nombu. In this Easter season, let the Risen Lord change us as Jonah's voice changed Nineveh.

Peter tells the first Christians not to be surprised at the fiery ordeal. If you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God because you bear this name (1 Peter 4:12, 16). Rejoice that you share the sufferings of Christ, for you will also share his glory.

When trouble comes for our faith, let us do what Peter says: entrust ourselves to the faithful Creator and keep on doing good (1 Peter 4:19). That is the sign of Jonah lived in our own life. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the story of Jonah? He was inside a big fish for three days, and then he came out! Jesus said he would be like Jonah: three days in the tomb, and then he would rise. And he did! When you see a picture of Jonah and the fish, remember: Jesus is alive!

intro: Theme: “For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.”
The sign of Jonah fulfilled in the Resurrection, the repentance of Nineveh, and the fiery ordeal borne with joy in the name of Christ.

points.h: No sign but the sign of Jonah
sub: A generation that asks for proof.
The sign already given: the empty tomb.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Make a simple act of faith in the Risen Lord today, without asking for any further sign.

sub: The queen who travelled to listen.
The One greater than Jonah and Solomon.
q: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Choose one thing to change this week because the Risen Lord has spoken to you.

points.h: Glorify God because you bear this name
sub: Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal.
Sharing Christ's sufferings, sharing his joy.
Entrust yourself and keep doing good.
q: See, I have refined you, but not like silver; I have tested you in the furnace of adversity.
Yet if any of you suffers as a Christian, do not consider it a disgrace, but glorify God because you bear this name.
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross openly before a meal, and pray each day this week for persecuted Christians.

concl: The Risen Christ is the one sign given to our generation, greater than Jonah and greater than Solomon.
Let us repent like Nineveh and bear his name with joy, even in the fire.
2027-04-26.resolve: This week, make an act of faith without conditions, change one thing at the Lord's word, and pray daily for those who suffer as Christians.
